name: MscStartup
evidence: __astart far-jumps here. DOS version check then DGROUP stack BSS zero InitRuntime _main _exit

name: __cintDIV
evidence: Interrupt 0 handler. Loads DGROUP and enters AmsgExit with message 3 (R6003 integer divide by 0)

name: AmsgExit
evidence: Prints the runtime banner and the message number in AX then _exit(255). __cintDIV falls into it and __chkstk jumps to it with AX 0 (R6000)

name: CintdivDgroup
evidence: Relocated DGROUP word read by __cintDIV before InitRuntime

name: InitRuntime
evidence: Far routine called from MscStartup. Installs the divide handler inherits _C_FILE_INFO into _osfile marks device handles and calls _initterm. MSC symbol for the whole function not confirmed

name: _exit
evidence: cx 0. Runs atexit terminators then DOS AH=4Ch. MscStartup calls it with the status from _main

name: __exit
evidence: cx 1. Skips atexit then DOS AH=4Ch. C _exit

name: _cexit
evidence: cx 0x100. Runs atexit then returns to the caller. C _cexit

name: __cexit
evidence: cx 0x101. Skips atexit and returns to the caller. C _c_exit

name: ExitCommon
evidence: Shared tail of _exit __exit _cexit and __cexit

name: ExitRestore
evidence: Near helper on the exit path. Restores interrupt 0 and the math error vector

name: _initterm
evidence: Calls each far pointer in a table from the top down skipping nulls. Later MSC _initterm walks upward

name: __chkstk
evidence: Far. Drops SP by AX under the return address. Overflow is R6000 through AmsgExit or the alternate handler

name: _main
evidence: MscStartup calls this after the three near pushes and before _exit. The bytes are enter 0x24, 0 and the rest of seg005, not a lone retf

name: NullStartup4
evidence: Single retf. Called from MscStartup. May be __fptrap or null __setenvp. See HANDOFF Unsure

name: NullStartup6
evidence: Single retf. Called from MscStartup. May be __FPMATH or null __setargv. See HANDOFF Unsure

name: __psp
evidence: Startup stores the incoming DS (the PSP) here and later reads the environment segment from it

name: _osfile
evidence: _C_FILE_INFO nibbles are stored here and the IOCTL loop sets the device bit on handles 0 to 4

name: __astart
evidence: EXE entry (e_ip). Microsoft C name for the startup; this copy sets up RTLink and jumps to the C startup in seg000

name: NotifySectionLoaded
evidence: Called after a section is marked resident; the body is nop then retf

name: ReleaseSection
evidence: Clears the resident flag, optionally fills the section with 8E8E, returns carry if pinned

name: LoadSection
evidence: Loads one overlay section and applies its relocations

name: OpenOverlayFile
evidence: Opens an overlay file or the EXE and keeps the DOS handle

name: LoadFromThunk
evidence: Target of every thunk's near call; loads the section named after the far jump

name: ZeroParagraphs
evidence: Zeros a run of paragraphs

name: MeasureThunkList
evidence: Finds where the overlay thunks start and end

name: CheckThunkList
evidence: Fatal eov0009 if the thunk list has changed

name: IsOverlayThunk
evidence: Recognises a call to LoadFromThunk followed by a far jump and a section index

name: ThunkListStart

name: ThunkListEnd

name: LoadSectionAl

name: OverlayReturnGate

name: PopReloadFrame

name: ReloadUnwind

name: InitOverlay

evidence: Eight bytes compared with the device name at offset 10 of the INT 67h vector

name: EndPtr
evidence: Far pointer ReadEndPtr returns. What writes it is not in this chunk. See HANDOFF

name: EndMark
evidence: Long stored by SetEndMark. WaitEnd spins until EndPtr passes it

name: CritRoutine
evidence: Far routine CritHandler calls. HookCrit stores the caller's pointer here

name: CritOld
evidence: INT 24h vector saved by HookCrit and restored by CritRestore

name: EmsMap
evidence: Near. INT 67h AH=44h. Maps CX logical pages from BX onto physical pages from AL

name: EmsMapRange
evidence: Maps a byte range into a free physical window and returns a pointer in the page frame

name: EmsMarkStale
evidence: Sets the high bit on the four EmsMapCache words

name: EmsInit
evidence: Checks EMMXXXX0, allocates pages, registers EmsFree with _onexit, then calls seg030. _main calls this

name: EmsFree
evidence: INT 67h AH=45h and stores -1. Registered with _onexit

name: EmsMapFrame
evidence: Maps four physical pages at the 16K page of the argument and returns a frame pointer

name: EmsSaveMap
evidence: Copies the four cached logical pages to a near buffer

name: EmsRestoreMap
evidence: Maps the four saved logical pages back onto physical pages 0-3

name: ReadEndPtr
evidence: Returns the far pointer at EndPtr. See HANDOFF

name: SetEndMark
evidence: Stores EndPtr plus the long argument at EndMark

name: WaitEnd
evidence: Spins until EndPtr is at or past EndMark

name: EndReached
evidence: AX is 1 when EndPtr is at or past EndMark

name: WaitAdd
evidence: Adds the long argument to EndPtr and spins until EndPtr reaches that sum

name: CopyFar
evidence: Far byte copy. Normalizes to a 32K window. Dword moves when the tested word is nonzero

name: CopyParas
evidence: Copies paragraphs from one segment to another, 64K at a time

name: CopyParasDown
evidence: Same copy from the top so an overlap moves downward

name: CritHandler
evidence: INT 24h handler. Far-calls CritRoutine

name: HookCrit
evidence: Saves INT 24h, points it at CritHandler, and registers CritRestore with _onexit. _main calls this

name: CritRestore
evidence: Restores INT 24h unless the saved segment word equals the saved offset word

name: SavedSp
evidence: ExitSavedSp uses this as SP when it is nonzero. What stores it is not in this chunk. See HANDOFF

name: PassFlag1
evidence: Sets SI from [bp+0Eh] and the flag byte to 1, then jumps to ArgSetup. Body at 0x29D2 is still incbin. See HANDOFF

name: PassFlag0
evidence: Sets SI from [bp+0Eh] and the flag byte to 0, then falls into ArgSetup

name: ArgSetup
evidence: Stores the arguments and jumps to offset 0x29D2, still incbin

name: AddrFlag0
evidence: Sets SI to the address of [bp+0Eh] and the flag byte to 0, then jumps to ArgSetup

name: AddrFlag1
evidence: Sets SI to the address of [bp+0Eh] and the flag byte to 1, then jumps to ArgSetup

name: OnexitThunk
evidence: jmp _onexit. EmsInit and HookCrit call this to register a routine

name: ExitSavedSp
evidence: Loads DGROUP, uses SavedSp as SP when that word is nonzero, then _exit(0). See HANDOFF

name: FileSizeArg
evidence: File length. The report-on-failure flag comes from the caller

name: FileSize
evidence: File length. A failed open returns 0

name: FileSizeMsg
evidence: File length. A failed open calls seg022. This is the far entry

name: FileSizeBody
evidence: Shared open, seek-to-end, close. Returns the length in DX:AX

name: PathBuf
evidence: FindPath returns this buffer. The directory is copied here and the DTA name is appended

name: PathCut
evidence: Offset in PathBuf just past the last colon or backslash

name: FindDta
evidence: DOS DTA for FindPath and FindNextPath. Set with INT 21h AH=1Ah

name: BlockEnd
evidence: Paragraph past the block AllocBytes allocated

name: BlockSeg
evidence: Segment AllocBytes got from INT 21h AH=48h

name: SavedCs
evidence: CS stored by AllocBytes. Not read in the bytes disassembled so far

name: SavedDs
evidence: DS stored by AllocBytes. Not read in the bytes disassembled so far

name: FileHeadArg
evidence: Reads four bytes. Failure flag comes from the caller. Result is bytes 1..3 divided by 16 rounded up

name: FileHead
evidence: Same as FileHeadArg with the failure flag forced to 0

name: FileHeadMsg
evidence: Same as FileHeadArg with the failure flag forced to 1. The seg022 call returns into FindPath

name: FileHeadBody
evidence: Open, read 4, close. Shifts the 24-bit value in bytes 1..3 right by 4 and adds 1 if the low nibble was set

name: FindPath
evidence: Findfirst attribute 6. Builds PathBuf from the directory and the DTA name. Returns PathBuf or 0

name: FindCopyName
evidence: Appends the 13-byte DTA name at PathCut and returns PathBuf

name: FindNone
evidence: Returns AX 0 through FindPath's epilogue

name: FindNextPath
evidence: Findnext, then FindCopyName. Returns 0 when the search ends

name: LargestFree
evidence: AH=48h BX=FFFFh. Returns the largest free block in bytes

name: AllocBytes
evidence: DX:AX is a byte size. Allocates that many paragraphs, or the largest block if the first try fails. Stores SavedCs SavedDs SavedSp

name: FoldScale
evidence: Folds a result into 0..100h and divides a word shifted left 14. Callees 0x1DD4 0x32EA 0x32F1 are still incbin. See HANDOFF

name: RetZero
evidence: xor ax, ax / retf

name: MapEsBx
evidence: Near. Calls EmsMarkStale, maps the long, returns ES:BX

name: PadSpace4
evidence: Near. After a 0, fills the rest of four bytes with spaces

name: LookupArg
evidence: 4-byte key lookup. Failure flag comes from the caller

name: Lookup
evidence: Same lookup with the failure flag forced to 0

name: LookupMsg
evidence: Same lookup with the failure flag forced to 1, which calls seg022

name: LookupBody
evidence: Maps the block, scans 4-byte records, and on a hit returns a long built from the record

name: FindFar
evidence: Looks up a long key in a far table. A miss returns 0 and does not call seg022

name: FindFarAlt
evidence: Same lookup. On a miss calls seg022 with the pointer at 0x6485

name: FindFarMsg
evidence: Same lookup. On a miss calls seg022 with the pointer at 0x645c. _main calls this

name: FindFarBody
evidence: Shared search. A hit returns the far pointer after the keys, added to DS

name: FindFarList
evidence: Walks keys until a 0 byte and stores each FindFarMsg result

name: FindFarQuiet
evidence: The same walk calling FindFar, so a miss stays quiet

name: FarToLinear
evidence: Far pointer on the stack to a 20-bit address in DX:AX

name: LinearToFar
evidence: 20-bit address on the stack to a far pointer whose offset is under 16

name: LinearToFarRegs
evidence: Same conversion with the low word in AX and the high word in DX

name: FmtSave
evidence: Four words FormatCall pops: far return offset, far return segment, then two arguments. See HANDOFF

name: FmtBuf
evidence: Pointer passed to _sprintf as its first argument from FormatCall

name: CopyBytes
evidence: Calls CopyFar. The byte count is the word at bp+0Eh and the high half is zero

name: FormatCall
evidence: Pops a far return and two words, calls _sprintf with FmtBuf, calls seg028, then far-returns. No far call lands here. See HANDOFF

name: ImulWords
evidence: Signed product of two stack words in DX:AX. Falls into ImulRegs

name: ImulRegs
evidence: imul dx / retf. Far calls land here

name: MulWords
evidence: Unsigned product of two stack words in DX:AX. Falls into MulRegs

name: MulRegs
evidence: mul dx / retf. Far calls land here

name: IdivWords
evidence: Signed DX:AX divided by the third stack word

name: DivWords
evidence: Unsigned DX:AX divided by the third stack word

name: Idiv32
evidence: Signed DX:AX divided by BX with a 32-bit idiv. Quotient returns in DX:AX

name: IdivDword
evidence: Stack dword divided by the stack word. High half cleared, then idiv. Quotient in DX:AX

name: WriteFile
evidence: Creates a file and writes a far buffer in 16K pieces. A short write deletes the file, then seg022 is called and AX is 0

name: WriteFileCode
evidence: Same write. Returns the DOS error, or 1 when a write was short

name: WriteFileBody
evidence: Shared create, write, close, and delete-on-failure path

name: RoundSeg
evidence: Adds (offset+15)/16 to the segment and clears AX

name: TableCount
evidence: Word at offset 4 of the far structure

name: TableAt
evidence: Far pointer for an entry index, or 0 past the count. Normalized like a FindFar hit

name: TableStore
evidence: Stores that entry dword through a near pointer, or stores 0

name: PathTail
evidence: DX:AX just past the last colon, at-sign, slash, or backslash in a near string

name: PathTailFar
evidence: Same scan of a far string

name: CopyStrN
evidence: Copies a near string, including the null, and stops at the null or the count

name: CopyStrNFar
evidence: Same copy from a far string

name: StrnDiff
evidence: Compares up to the count. AX is 0 when the bytes match through a null, else 1
